extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: NeedleBench is a customizable synthetic bilingual long-context benchmark/framework for evaluating LLM retrieval and reasoning across varying information densities. It includes information-sparse tasks (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Reasoning) and the information-dense Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC), with adaptive context lengths from 4k to 1000k and beyond.
extraction.creator: Mo Li; Songyang Zhang; Taolin Zhang; Haodong Duan; Yunxin Liu; Kai Chen
extraction.citeAs: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen. NeedleBench: Evaluating LLM Retrieval and Reasoning Across Varying Information Densities. Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 09/2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is programmatically constructed as a synthetic framework. Information-sparse tasks are built by inserting synthetic fictional 'needles' into long-context 'haystack' filler text at varying depths and context lengths. The information-dense ATC task is generated algorithmically by sampling unique names, assigning relationship terms and templates, shuffling relationship statements, creating question prompts, and computing ground-truth answers. The benchmark is bilingual, with English and Chinese task variants.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection; Experiments; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic, abstract, fictional statements and relational facts are used as needles. For English haystack filler, passages are taken from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset. For Chinese haystack filler, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used. The ATC task uses synthetic family relationship data generated from name pools, relationship vocabularies, and linguistic templates.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Needles are strategically inserted at various depths within contexts of different target lengths. For ATC, relationship statements are randomly shuffled to eliminate positional bias. Context length is varied by changing the number of needles from 2 to 512. A buffer is subtracted from target context length during input generation to mitigate instruction truncation caused by tokenizer discrepancies.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Multi-Needle Reasoning, model predictions are post-processed to extract only the content inside \boxed{...}. Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer. During generation, a buffer is subtracted from the target context length so all models receive complete instructions despite tokenizer differences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth labels are created programmatically. For information-sparse tasks, predefined sets of core keywords are used for keyword-aware exact match scoring. For ATC, the generation algorithm computes the ground-truth answer from the constructed family structure. In addition, the authors manually annotated approximately 10% of observed ATC errors for error analysis, focusing on the 'identifying the eldest ancestor' question type.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes annotation/evaluation through predefined keyword-aware exact match for sparse tasks and exact match on required \boxed{...} format for ATC. The authors also manually annotated about 10% of ATC errors and categorized them into under-thinking, partial understanding, instruction following, repetitive output, hallucination, and other errors. They further analyzed output-format compliance and found false errors due to missing \boxed{...} formatting only in two small models and only in the simplest setting.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All codes and resources are publicly available at OpenCompass. The paper also states that all reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Names; family relationships; language (English and Chinese). The names and relationships are synthetic and fictional.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide targeted evaluation tools for understanding and improving long-context capabilities of LLMs, especially for real-world applications such as legal document retrieval, academic research, and business intelligence. The paper highlights the importance of targeted assessments for identifying gaps in models' ability to manage information-dense scenarios and suggests future work to improve reasoning strategies and mitigate under-thinking.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that benchmarks derived from real-world texts risk contamination from models' prior knowledge or pretraining overlap, which can undermine fair assessment. NeedleBench uses largely synthetic tasks to mitigate this confound. The authors also report a performance gap between English and Chinese for most models, with English typically higher, and suggest this may relate to pretraining data distribution, tokenization strategies, or language-specific modeling approaches.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The paper notes that realistic benchmarks may be saturated and reflect memorization, while synthetic tasks are necessary for valid evaluation, but future work should expand NeedleBench to cover more diverse and realistic information-dense scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Use case is evaluation/benchmarking of large language models for long-context retrieval and reasoning, including bilingual assessment under information-sparse and information-dense settings. It is used for testing model performance across adaptive context lengths, needle depths, reasoning complexity, and cross-lingual scenarios.
